I am 62 this year, and I have been farming this land in Quzhou for 35 years. I finished middle school, so I can read fertilizer bags and do my own accounts, but most of what I know comes from doing it and watching others. I talk to dealer Lao Zhang at the input shop and I watch my neighbors, especially Old Wang, because if his cotton does well, I copy him. With only two people in my household and 12 mu total, I keep things practical: I manage 5 mu of winter wheat that will turn into summer maize after the June harvest, and 7 mu of cotton that stays in the ground from spring to autumn.

Right now it is spring, so my wheat is already greening up. Last autumn I ploughed that plot deep and put down 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as basal. Looking at the field this year, I remember last season I only topdressed once with 20 jin of urea and the grain was a bit light. This year I will topdress twice: 20 jin of urea per mu at green-up and another 20 jin at jointing. I will not add more phosphorus or potassium in spring; what I put down in autumn is enough. I will irrigate three times from the well—green-up, jointing, and grain filling—because pumping costs electricity but losing yield costs more. Two sprays: one for aphids and one for powdery mildew if the humidity rises. I sow an improved wheat variety that Lao Zhang stocks every year. I expect about 500 kg per mu.

For cotton, which is my cash crop on 7 mu, I buy fresh hybrid seed every spring, about 3 jin per mu, because saved seed loses vigor. Before sowing in late April I plough the field and apply 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as basal. At first flowering I will topdress with 30 jin of urea per mu, and at peak flowering I will add another 20 jin of urea plus 20 jin of potassium sulfate. Old Wang did exactly that last year and his cotton stayed green until October, so I am doing the same. I will irrigate three times: once after sowing if the soil is dry, once at flowering, and once at boll stage. Four sprays total: a herbicide before sowing, then insecticide for aphids, then for red spider mites, and one more if bollworm shows up. I expect 250 kg of seed cotton per mu.

After I cut the wheat in early June, I will rotary till that same 5 mu quickly and plant hybrid maize seed the same day. There is no time to deep plough between wheat and maize. I will put 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing, and at the big trumpet stage I will topdress with 50 jin of urea per mu. That gives the maize a strong push when it needs it most. I will irrigate twice—once at sowing if it is dry, and once at big trumpet—and spray twice: a herbicide right after sowing and an insecticide for corn borer later. I expect 600 kg per mu.

Fertilizer prices went up again this year, and I feel it every time I pay Lao Zhang. But I learned long ago that I would rather apply a bit too much than risk a bad harvest. A thin crop is a disaster; an extra bag of urea is just a cost I can live with. I start from what I did last year, adjust based on what I saw in the field and what my neighbors bought, and I never change everything at once because change is risky.
